pages.title: OP-17 The World's Strongest Warriors — Official Release Facts & Sealed Box Research
pages.description: Official OP-17 Japanese and English release dates, pack pricing, 131+4 card types, confirmed treatments, and the limits of pre-release sealed box data.
pages.headline: OP-17 “The World's Strongest Warriors”: official release facts and sealed box research
pages.introHtml: This page separates published product facts from pre-release market observations. Bandai's English product page confirms the August 28 release, August 21 pre-release, USD $4.99 pack price, and 131+4 card types. Shueisha's official Shonen Jump card page lists the Japanese release on August 22 at ¥240 per six-card pack. OP Box Index does not publish a sealed-box market price until completed-sale data exists.
facts: Pre-release · no post-release sold sample yet
pages.sourceHtml: Sources checked August 10, 2026: Bandai's official English product page and Shueisha's official Shonen Jump card page. Region-specific dates and prices are kept separate.

sections.heading: What the official pages establish
paragraphsHtml: Bandai identifies OP-17 as the fourth-anniversary main booster and shows the English product's release schedule, price, total card-type count, and rarity families. The official page also presents Elbaf, the Rocks Pirates, and the Four Emperors as product themes. Those are product facts; they do not establish a secondary-market value.

The Japanese and English editions are separate products. The ¥240 Japanese pack figure must not be compared directly with a USD $4.99 English pack without accounting for pack contents, language, taxes, shipping, and local distribution. A retailer's display-box asking price is also not the same thing as Bandai's per-pack suggested price.

sections.heading: OP-17 box price, reprint status and factory-seal checks
paragraphsHtml: Before release, most visible box prices are retailer or marketplace asks. They are not completed sales, and cancelled orders, deposits, allocation uncertainty, or mixed Japanese and English listings can distort them. For that reason, this page does not turn pre-order asks into a market median or a buy recommendation.

No source-backed OP-17 reprint can exist before the product's first Japanese release. Later restocks will be recorded only when a dated retailer or distributor source is available; pre-order inventory and rumours will not be relabelled as reprints.

For the Japanese display, the factory-seal standard is the original Bandai security tape in uncut condition. Added shrink does not replace that tape. The older launch pages for OP-14, OP-15, and OP-16 provide historical context, but their price paths do not predict OP-17. Once OP-17 has a valid sold sample, its own observation count, range, language, and date will appear here.

sections.heading: Confirmed card treatments, without price projections
paragraphsHtml: Bandai's product presentation confirms a Super Leader Alt-Art treatment and identifies OP17-079 Monkey.D.Luffy as the shown example. It also presents Super Alt-Art cards, Treasure Rare, Special Cards, and anniversary-themed treatments. These details help identify the product, but no raw-card or PSA 10 value is assigned before matched sales exist.

Card reveals can change which listings attract attention, but attention is not a measured sale. Individual card pages are added only after the artwork, card number, language, condition, and sale record can be matched.

sections.heading: How to verify a sealed display
paragraphsHtml: For a Japanese One Piece display, the primary factory-seal check is the original Bandai security tape in uncut condition. Added shrink is not a substitute for that tape. Photos should show the top tape, both side seams, bottom, product code, and any dents or tears. English displays use their region's factory wrapping and labeling, so the two seal standards should not be mixed.

A marketplace listing should also state the language and quantity clearly. Loose packs, opened displays, mixed-language lots, and listings that hide the seal area are excluded from OP Box Index's sealed-box comparisons.

sections.heading: When this page changes
paragraphsHtml: After the Japanese and English releases, the page will add verified sold-price summaries only when the sample meets the rules in our methodology. Chase-card tables require matched printings, and grading figures remain population reports rather than estimates of how many sealed boxes were opened. Every material update receives a new visible review date.

faq: When does OP-17 release?
Shueisha's official card page lists August 22, 2026 for Japan. Bandai lists an August 21 English pre-release and August 28 English release.
What is the official OP-17 pack price?
The cited Japanese page lists ¥240 for a six-card pack. Bandai's English page lists USD $4.99 per pack. These are region-specific pack figures, not a secondary-market box quote.
What is an OP-17 sealed box worth before release?
No post-release sold sample exists yet. Pre-order asking prices are recorded separately and are not presented as established market value.
What seal should a Japanese OP-17 display have?
The original Bandai security tape should be present and uncut. Added shrink does not replace that factory-seal evidence.
Why is there no buy rating yet?
A rating before release would rely on asking prices and assumptions rather than completed-sale evidence. This page waits for a dated, language-matched sample.

pages.title: EB-05 Heroines Edition Vol.2 — Official Product Facts & Data Limits
pages.description: Official EB-05 Heroines Edition vol.2 release window, English pack price and contents, plus the evidence still needed for sealed-box valuation.
pages.headline: EB-05 “Heroines Edition vol.2”: official product facts and data limits
pages.introHtml: Bandai's official English product page confirms EB-05 as the second Heroines Extra Booster, with an October 2026 release window, USD $4.99 pack price, and 12 cards per pack. The same page does not yet publish an exact day, total card count, full card list, or Japanese display specification. This guide keeps those missing fields open instead of filling them with retailer assumptions.
facts: EXTRA BOOSTER -ONE PIECE HEROINES EDITION vol.2- [EB-05]
Not listed on the official page checked
pages.sourceHtml: Source checked August 10, 2026: Bandai's official EB-05 product page. Exact-day retailer listings are not treated as official confirmation.

sections.heading: Confirmed information and open fields
paragraphsHtml: The official page establishes the product name, October release month, English pack price, and 12-card pack contents. It also describes EB-05 as the second Heroines Extra Booster. It does not provide a rarity breakdown, card-type total, exact English release day, or a Japanese-language product specification as of the review date.

Those gaps matter for sealed-box research. English pack contents cannot be copied into a Japanese display entry, and an exact date shown by a shop can change before Bandai updates its own product page. OP Box Index therefore labels the month as confirmed and the remaining fields as pending.

sections.heading: What EB-03 can and cannot tell us
paragraphsHtml: EB-03 Heroines Edition is the closest thematic comparison because it is the first product in the same named line. Its live page contains the current sealed-box observations and chase-card data. Keeping that changing data on the EB-03 page avoids freezing an old price into this preview.

One predecessor is a sample of one. Differences in card list, print volume, distribution, release timing, and reprints can produce a different result for EB-05. EB-03's history is useful context, but it is not evidence that EB-05 demand or price will follow the same path.

sections.heading: Evidence required before a sealed-box valuation
paragraphsHtml: A useful EB-05 valuation needs the official Japanese and English specifications, confirmed card list and treatments, language-matched completed sales, transaction counts, and a clear seal condition. Active listings may show seller expectations, but they are not substituted for sales. Card prices also do not automatically equal sealed-box value because pull rates and hit distribution must be known.
Reprint information is reported only when Bandai, distributors, or dated market supply records support it. Absence of a reprint notice is not described as proof that no reprint will occur.

sections.heading: How to verify a Japanese sealed display
paragraphsHtml: For a Japanese One Piece display, require clear photos of the original Bandai security tape and confirm that it is uncut. Added shrink does not replace the tape check. Inspect the box code, top and bottom panels, side seams, dents, tears, and any adhesive irregularity. Loose packs, opened displays, mixed-language lots, and listings that conceal the tape are excluded.
The official English page describes packs, not a Japanese display seal. Product language and seal standard must therefore be recorded separately rather than inferred from the Heroines name.

sections.heading: Update policy
paragraphsHtml: This page will be reviewed when Bandai publishes additional specifications, the card list appears, or a valid sold-box sample forms. Material changes receive a new visible review date. Price, population, and reprint fields follow the definitions in our methodology; unavailable values remain unavailable.

faq: When does EB-05 release?
Bandai's official English page lists October 2026. It did not list an exact day when checked on August 10, 2026.
What is the official English pack price?
Bandai lists USD $4.99 per pack, with 12 cards in an English pack.
How many card types are in EB-05?
The official page checked on August 10 did not list a total card-type count or full card list.
Does EB-03 predict EB-05's sealed-box price?
No. EB-03 is a relevant thematic comparison, but one predecessor cannot establish EB-05 demand, supply, or future price.
What seal should a Japanese EB-05 display have?
Use the original uncut Bandai security tape as the primary factory-seal check. Do not use added shrink as a substitute.
